item.title: Open VSX Extension ID Reuse and Service-Specific Infostealer Credential Markets
item.content:encoded:
Window: 24 Aug 02:00 → 24 Aug 06:00 UTC (4 hours)

Open VSX Unblocks Extension IDs Used in Malware Campaign — Should Read

Open VSX unblocked three extension IDs that had been abused in an evil-twin malware campaign so legitimate maintainers could reclaim and publish them. The case shows why teams should track extension versions, hashes, publishers, and repositories—not just extension IDs—because a once-malicious name can later point to legitimate software.

  • Open VSX unblocked the extension IDs AlDuncanson.react-hooks-snippets, magne-sjaastad.opm-flow-editor-support, and rumbledb.jsoniq-vscode between August 16 and August 20 after all three had been used by impostors in a 77-extension evil-twin campaign documented by Manifold Security.
  • Legitimate versions of OPM Flow Editor Support and RumbleDB's JSONiq and XQuery extension are now live on Open VSX, while React Hooks Snippets had been unblocked but did not yet have a legitimate Open VSX listing as of publication.
  • Open VSX had removed all 77 malicious packages by August 3 and added their IDs to its malicious-extension list, but the legitimate publishers were not compromised and were not involved in the campaign.
  • The article says Open VSX's malicious-extension list stores only extension ID strings, which becomes ambiguous when a legitimate owner reclaims an ID that was previously used for malicious code.
  • The article recommends that organizations using Open VSX record extension IDs together with exact versions, file hashes, publisher identities, and source repositories so historical deny rules remain tied to the malicious artifact rather than the reused name.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: open-vsx, vs-code-marketplace, visual-studio-code, react-hooks-snippets, opm-flow-editor-support, jsoniq-vscode, carbon-vscode

Vendors: eclipse-foundation, microsoft, socket, manifold-security, rumbledb, carbon-language

The Rise of Service-Centric Credential Compilations — Optional

Cybercriminals are increasingly turning raw infostealer logs into service-specific packages that bundle credentials with cookies, tokens, and session data, making account takeover faster and more reliable. The biggest concern is AI platforms like ChatGPT, where stolen sessions can expose sensitive corporate knowledge and require defenders to protect and revoke active sessions, not just passwords.

  • Cybercriminals are increasingly organizing raw infostealer logs into service-specific compilations focused on platforms such as ChatGPT, Netflix, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and social media services.
  • These curated packages may include credentials, browser cookies, persistent session cookies, refresh tokens, JWTs, CSRF tokens, device identifiers, and other authentication artifacts recovered from victims’ browsers.
  • Initial Access Brokers are enriching stolen information by combining fresh credentials from infostealer infections with browser artifacts, session cookies, and authentication tokens before selling it to other criminals.
  • Compromised AI platform accounts can expose sensitive corporate knowledge, proprietary source code, strategic business plans, financial analysis, legal documents, internal procedures, and confidential conversations.
  • The article recommends rapid session invalidation and token revocation, continuous monitoring of exposed identities, adaptive MFA and device-risk analysis, and visibility into underground marketplaces where service-centric compilations are traded.

Technologies: cloud-platform, browser, iam, mfa

Products: chatgpt, netflix, microsoft-365, google-workspace, claude, gemini

Vendors: openai, netflix, microsoft, google, anthropic

item.title: Compromised Vendor Microsoft 365 Mailbox Used in Thread-Hijacked Voicemail Phish
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Aug 10:00 → 23 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

A Real Thread, a Real Mailbox, One Swapped Button — Should Read

A compromised vendor Microsoft 365 mailbox sent a phishing voicemail lure embedded in a real prior internal thread, allowing SPF, DKIM, DMARC and ARC to pass and making the message look trustworthy. The key risk is that valid vendor accounts can bypass sender-based trust signals, so payload links and user reports must be evaluated independently of authentication results.

  • A resident-services staff member at a residential property management company received a voicemail playback notice in mid-August 2026 from a vendor mailbox her employer had corresponded with before.
  • The email was sent from the vendor’s own Microsoft 365 tenant, and SPF, DKIM, DMARC, both ARC seals, and composite authentication all passed under the vendor’s domain.
  • The message reused a genuine internal vendor support thread from the previous day, including real staff signatures and working vendor links, while adding only a new voicemail playback block.
  • The two call-to-action buttons in the fake voicemail block both resolved through Microsoft link rewriting to hxxps://reikongaku[.]com/voicewavcalerIDsms/.
  • The recipient reported the message herself, the report was approved manually, and the affected mailbox was quarantined roughly three days after the send.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-365, adaptive-ai

Vendors: microsoft, ironscales

item.title: CVE-2026-21580 Enables Unauthenticated Stored XSS Privilege Escalation in Atlassian Confluence
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Aug 02:00 → 23 Aug 06:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-21580) Confluence Privilege Escalation via Unauthenticated Stored XSS — Must Read

CVE-2026-21580 is a critical unauthenticated stored XSS flaw in self-hosted Atlassian Confluence Data Center and Server that can let attackers execute code in an admin’s browser and escalate privileges. Organizations should urgently inventory exposed Confluence instances, restrict access, and upgrade to fixed releases.

  • CVE-2026-21580 is a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Data Center and Server that Atlassian groups with a privilege escalation component and a security misconfiguration weakness.
  • Exploitation does not require authentication, and an attacker with network access to a vulnerable Confluence instance can plant a payload that later runs in the browser of a user who views the affected content.
  • The vulnerability has a CVSS 4.0 base score of 8.6, while Atlassian labels it Critical under its own advisory taxonomy.
  • Atlassian lists affected Confluence Data Center and Server releases spanning 7.1.1 through 10.2.0, while Confluence Cloud is not in scope.
  • Atlassian has published fixed releases and recommends upgrading to the latest Confluence Data Center and Server version, with 9.2.21 or later and 10.2.13 or later named as supported fixed versions for maintained lines.

Technologies: cms

Products: confluence-data-center, confluence-server, cycognito-platform

Vendors: atlassian, cycognito

item.title: Intuit Notification Redirect Used to Camouflage Fresh .icu Credential Theft Domain
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Aug 10:00 → 22 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

A Real Intuit Notification Link, Then a 7-Day-Old Domain — Should Read

Attackers used a legitimate Intuit notification redirect as a trusted first hop to send victims to a seven-day-old credential-harvesting domain, allowing the link to appear clean to reputation-based scanners. The key lesson is to analyze the full redirect chain and terminal destination, not just the authenticated email or reputable initial URL.

  • A regional financial services company and its mortgage-lending affiliate received a generic document-share email from a personal free-mail account with a single “read the message” button.
  • The button first resolved through links.notification.intuit.com, a genuine Intuit notification and click-tracking host, before forwarding to account-maildocuments-xsaas.icu.
  • The terminal domain account-maildocuments-xsaas.icu had been registered through NameSilo seven days before the email was sent and used Cloudflare nameservers.
  • The message passed DKIM, DMARC, composite authentication, and ARC, while the SPF softfail was described as a relay artifact rather than evidence of spoofing.
  • IRONSCALES Themis scored the message at 84% confidence for credential theft, and four affected mailboxes were quarantined and reverted roughly seventeen minutes after delivery.

Technologies: email-security

Products: gmail, themis

Vendors: intuit, google, microsoft, namesilo, cloudflare, ironscales

item.title: NetSPI Introduces EchoBench Benchmark for Autonomous AI Web Application Pentesting
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Aug 22:00 → 22 Aug 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

Introducing EchoBench: A Human Calibrated Benchmark for Autonomous Pentesting — Optional

NetSPI introduced EchoBench, a benchmark that evaluates autonomous web application pentesting systems by comparing their validated findings against a measured cohort of human associate pentesters. Its main value is giving AI pentesting scores a human-calibrated denominator, with performance broken down by fidelity, difficulty, OWASP coverage, and repeatability.

  • NetSPI introduced EchoBench as an empirically calibrated human outcome benchmark for evaluating autonomous AI web application pentesting systems.
  • An ECHO score of 100 represents parity with a measured human cohort that currently consists of associate pentesters from NetSPI University.
  • EchoBench scores a model and its harness configuration together across four components: finding fidelity, difficulty-reach, OWASP breadth, and repeatability.
  • The current benchmark corpus contains five web applications and 184 canonical finding IDs, with 173 findings currently assigned human difficulty labels.
  • Every published EchoBench score is intended to include the human reference cohort, benchmark version, ground truth, evaluation rules, model, harness, target versions, run budget, component values, provenance views, and repeat coverage.

Products: echobench

Vendors: netspi, owasp

item.title: Identity Verification Testing and Agentic AI Data Security Platform Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Aug 18:00 → 21 Aug 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Verifying the Verifier – Assessing Identity Verification Services — Optional

Identity verification systems that use AI, biometrics, documents, or voice checks must be tested like any other security-critical system because attackers can use synthetic IDs, deepfake voices, and spoofed environments to bypass them. A strong assessment compares legitimate baseline behavior against adversarial submissions and infrastructure checks to find weaknesses before real fraud occurs.

  • An Identity Verification assessment evaluates whether an identity verification system can accurately validate presented identities and whether its underlying infrastructure securely handles sensitive information.
  • NetSPI’s methodology includes data aggregation and synthetic data creation, reconnaissance, baseline validation, adversarial testing, and reporting observations.
  • Synthetic test data may include altered identity documents, swapped faces, changed birth dates or identification numbers, and deepfake voice recordings created from original control data.
  • During adversarial testing, assessors submit synthetic identities and look for bypasses, responses to spoofed device or sensor conditions, and sensitive data in network or HTTP traffic.
  • The final report includes platform-specific findings, reproducible proof-of-concept steps, and mitigation strategies based on industry best practices and standards such as NIST 800-63-3.

Technologies: iam, identity-provider

Products: netspi-security-testing-identity-verification

Vendors: netspi

3 Takeaways from Forrester’s 2026 Data Security Platforms Landscape Report — Optional

Forrester’s 2026 Data Security Platforms report argues that AI agents are pushing data security platforms beyond visibility and discovery toward automated enforcement and remediation. The key takeaway is that enterprises need DSPs that can continuously control data access and usage at scale, not just dashboards that identify risk.

  • Forrester published The Data Security Platforms Landscape, Q3 2026, profiling 31 vendors and describing the data security platform category as mature.
  • The article says agentic AI is both the main trend and top disruptor for data security platforms because AI agents access data at machine speed, generate data, and act autonomously.
  • The article says buyers face a persistent gap between fragmented visibility and accountable remediation while keeping data usable.
  • The article argues that data security platforms must go beyond data security posture management by enforcing policies for data access, use, and lifecycle management.
  • The article says Forrester’s landscape includes database activity monitoring and data-centric threat detection as core capabilities of a data security platform.

Vendors: forrester, varonis

item.title: Extortion Email Abuses Retired Vendor Domain and DMARC Enforcement Gap
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Aug 10:00 → 21 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Retired Brand, Real Signature: Extortion in a DMARC Gap — Should Read

An extortion email reached inboxes because it authenticated with SPF and DKIM for a vendor’s current domain while the visible From address used the vendor’s retired legacy domain, causing DMARC alignment to fail without enforcement. The attached “breach proof” was real but unrelated old personal injury paperwork, showing how recycled sensitive documents and rebrand-related authentication gaps can make social engineering more convincing.

  • A shared scheduling mailbox at a workers'-compensation and care-management services company received an extortion email with the subject "Data leak !" claiming 700 gigabytes of company data would be published.
  • The email passed SPF and DKIM for an enterprise analytics vendor's current domain, but DMARC failed because the visible From address used the same vendor's retired pre-rebrand domain.
  • Microsoft composite authentication returned a pass despite the DMARC failure with no enforcement, allowing the message to reach the inbox.
  • The message contained no links, executable content, or payment portal, and used a qTox messenger ID as the only negotiation channel.
  • Two inspected images offered as breach proof contained genuine but unrelated third-party personal injury records from nearly a decade earlier, not proof of a breach at the recipient organization.

Technologies: email-security

Products: adaptive-ai, qtox, microsoft-composite-authentication

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, qtox

item.title: MoYu Android head-unit malware, AI vulnerability benchmarks, and ransomware endpoint blind spots
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Aug 06:00 → 21 Aug 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

The invisible passenger in your car — Must Read

Kaspersky found Android malware being delivered through the legitimate update mechanism of DoFun automotive head units, turning car infotainment systems into ad-fraud and proxy-botnet nodes. The campaign is attributed with high confidence to MoYu Group, a BADBOX-linked threat actor.

  • Kaspersky discovered a new Android multi-stage downloader in June 2026 whose ultimate purpose is ad fraud and creation of a proxy botnet.
  • The malware spread through the built-in updaters of Android-based automotive head unit firmware, using the legitimate TWCore system application to install APK files on affected devices.
  • The first-stage JarService dropper had no user interface and decrypted embedded data to load a second-stage malicious loader, which then contacted attacker servers to download a third-stage payload.
  • The third-stage payload could receive commands to make HTTP requests, open links in WebView, execute JavaScript, download additional code, and load the zhima reverse proxy module.
  • Kaspersky attributed the activity with high confidence to MoYu Group, an actor linked to the BADBOX botnet, based on naming patterns and infrastructure overlap.

Technologies: mobile-os, iot-device, message-queue, proxy

Products: android, twcore, dofun-head-units, jarservice, zhima, badbox, pxyedge, proxyforu

Vendors: kaspersky, dofun, google, pxyedge, proxyforu

We burned 11.7bn tokens to find the best cyber AI model — May Read

Aikido benchmarked 10 AI models on rediscovering 32 fresh vulnerabilities and found that repeated runs of cheaper open-weight models, especially DeepSeek V4 Pro, achieved the best recall. The key trade-off is that these models found more bugs for less money but generated more false leads, making strong harnessing and triage essential.

  • Aikido benchmarked 10 AI models on 32 recently disclosed vulnerabilities, running each model across the full dataset three times without internet access.
  • DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 achieved the highest pooled recall, finding 28 of 32 vulnerabilities across three runs.
  • Pooling repeated runs improved coverage for several models, with DeepSeek Pro rising from 17 vulnerabilities in its first pass to 28 across three, Qwen from 19 to 26, Kimi from 17 to 25, and Grok from 24 to 26.
  • Grok 4.6 was the most consistent model tested, finding 21 vulnerabilities in all three runs, while Opus 5 and GPT Sol each consistently found 19.
  • The article says cheaper open models can match or beat public closed frontier models in pooled recall, but they also produced more false leads that the pipeline had to reject.

Products: deepseek-v4-pro-0813, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, glm-5.3, qwen3.8-max, kimi-k3, grok-4.6, opus-5, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-sol, aikido-ai-code-analysis, code-security-audit, aikido-attack

Vendors: aikido, deepseek, z-ai, alibaba, moonshot-ai, xai, anthropic, openai

Endpoint Blind Spots: The 5 Places Ransomware Hides Before It Detonates — Optional

Ransomware often hides in endpoint blind spots such as remote access tools, stolen credentials, vendor connections, OT systems, and compromised business email before encryption begins. Organizations should focus on early detection with MFA, least privilege, segmentation, patching, backups, and broad endpoint monitoring.

  • Ransomware attackers often spend time before encryption establishing access, stealing credentials, moving laterally, and identifying valuable systems.
  • Legitimate remote access tools such as WinSCP, AnyDesk, and ScreenConnect have been abused by Qilin affiliates to facilitate lateral movement.
  • Compromised endpoints can expose credential stores, and ransomware operators have used credential-harvesting techniques associated with tools such as NirSoft and Mimikatz.
  • Vendor connections and supply chain access can let attackers compromise a smaller vendor and use a trusted relationship to reach a larger target.
  • Operational technology and industrial control systems in manufacturing environments can be difficult to patch and may create endpoint security blind spots.

Technologies: edr, antivirus, remote-access, mfa, ics-scada

Products: cyble-titan, cyble-vision, blaze-ai, winscp, anydesk, screenconnect, nirsoft, mimikatz

Vendors: cyble, winscp, anydesk, connectwise, nirsoft
